# Diagnostic flags in Clang

## Introduction

This page lists the diagnostic flags currently supported by Clang.

:::{role} warning
:class: warning
:::

:::{role} diagtext
:class: diagtext
:::

:::{role} error
:class: error
:::

:::{role} remark
:class: remark
:::

% Based on `emphasis` so that adjacent placeholders stay separate elements
% instead of merging into one `*A**B*` emphasis run.
:::{role} placeholder(emphasis)
:::

## Diagnostic flags

(-W)=

### -W

Synonym for {ref}`-Wextra`.


(-W#pragma-messages)=

### -W#pragma-messages

This diagnostic is enabled by default.

**Diagnostic text:**

The text of this diagnostic is not controlled by Clang.


(-W#warnings)=

### -W#warnings

This diagnostic is enabled by default.

**Diagnostic text:**

The text of this diagnostic is not controlled by Clang.


(-WCFString-literal)=

### -WCFString-literal

This diagnostic is enabled by default.

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`input conversion stopped due to an input byte that does not belong to the input codeset UTF-8`
:::


(-WCL4)=

### -WCL4

Some of the diagnostics controlled by this flag are enabled by default.

Controls {ref}`-Wall`, {ref}`-Wextra`.


(-WIndependentClass-attribute)=

### -WIndependentClass-attribute

This diagnostic is enabled by default.

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`'objc_independent_class' attribute may be put on a typedef only; attribute is ignored`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`'objc_independent_class' attribute may be put on Objective-C object pointer type only; attribute is ignored`
:::

(-Wabi)=

### -Wabi

This diagnostic flag exists for GCC compatibility, and has no effect in Clang.

(-Wabsolute-value)=

### -Wabsolute-value

This diagnostic is enabled by default.

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`absolute value function`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`given an argument of type`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`&nbsp;{diagtext}`but has parameter of type`&nbsp;{placeholder}`C`&nbsp;{diagtext}`which may cause truncation of value`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`taking the absolute value of`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`pointer`
    * - {diagtext}`function`
    * - {diagtext}`array`
    :::
  - &nbsp;{diagtext}`type`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`&nbsp;{diagtext}`is suspicious`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`taking the absolute value of unsigned type`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`has no effect`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`using`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`integer`
    * - {diagtext}`floating point`
    * - {diagtext}`complex`
    :::
  - &nbsp;{diagtext}`absolute value function`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`when argument is of`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`integer`
    * - {diagtext}`floating point`
    * - {diagtext}`complex`
    :::
  - &nbsp;{diagtext}`type`
:::

### -Wcstring-format-directive

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`NSString`
    * - {diagtext}`CFString`
    :::
  - &nbsp;{diagtext}`which is being passed as a formatting argument to the formatting`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`method`
    * - {diagtext}`CFfunction`
    :::
:::

:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`imported AST from '`{placeholder}`A`{diagtext}`' had been generated for a different target, current:`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`{diagtext}`, imported:`&nbsp;{placeholder}`C`
:::

:widths: auto

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

(-Wdeprecated)=

### -Wdeprecated

Some of the diagnostics controlled by this flag are enabled by default.

Also controls {ref}`-Wdeprecated-anon-enum-enum-conversion`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-array-compare`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-attributes`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-builtins`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-comma-subscript`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-copy`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-copy-with-dtor`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-declarations`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-dynamic-exception-spec`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-enum-compare`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-enum-compare-conditional`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-enum-enum-conversion`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-enum-float-conversion`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-increment-bool`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-literal-operator`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-missing-comma-variadic-parameter`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-octal-literals`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-ofast`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-pragma`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-redundant-constexpr-static-def`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-register`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-this-capture`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-type`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-volatile`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-writable-strings`.

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`-O4 is equivalent to -O3`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`access declarations are deprecated; use using declarations instead`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`argument '`{placeholder}`A`{diagtext}`' is deprecated`
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * -
    * - {diagtext}`, use '`{placeholder}`C`{diagtext}`' instead`
    :::
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`argument '`{placeholder}`A`{diagtext}`' is deprecated,`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`treating '`{placeholder}`A`{diagtext}`' input as '`{placeholder}`B`{diagtext}`' when in C++ mode, this behavior is deprecated`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`'default' clause for 'metadirective' is deprecated; use 'otherwise' instead`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`'depend' clause for 'ordered' is deprecated; use 'doacross' instead`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`the delimited form of '#pragma omp declare target' without clauses is deprecated; use '#pragma omp begin declare target' instead`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`minus(-) operator for reductions is deprecated; use + or user defined reduction instead`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`does not support the option '`{placeholder}`B`{diagtext}`'`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`use of 'long' with '__vector' is deprecated`
:::

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

:widths: auto

(-Wdocumentation)=

### -Wdocumentation

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`'`
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`\\`
    * - {diagtext}`@`
    :::
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`class`
    * - {diagtext}`interface`
    * - {diagtext}`protocol`
    * - {diagtext}`struct`
    * - {diagtext}`union`
    :::
  - {diagtext}`' command should not be used in a comment attached to a non-`
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`class`
    * - {diagtext}`interface`
    * - {diagtext}`protocol`
    * - {diagtext}`struct`
    * - {diagtext}`union`
    :::
  - &nbsp;{diagtext}`declaration`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`duplicated command '`
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`\\`
    * - {diagtext}`@`
    :::
  - {placeholder}`B`{diagtext}`'`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`empty paragraph passed to '`
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`\\`
    * - {diagtext}`@`
    :::
  - {placeholder}`B`{diagtext}`' command`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`'`
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`\\`
    * - {diagtext}`@`
    :::
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`classdesign`
    * - {diagtext}`coclass`
    * - {diagtext}`dependency`
    * - {diagtext}`helper`
    * - {diagtext}`helperclass`
    * - {diagtext}`helps`
    * - {diagtext}`instancesize`
    * - {diagtext}`ownership`
    * - {diagtext}`performance`
    * - {diagtext}`security`
    * - {diagtext}`superclass`
    :::
  - {diagtext}`' command should not be used in a comment attached to a non-container declaration`

(-Wexperimental-lifetime-safety-field-origin-escape)=

### -Wexperimental-lifetime-safety-field-origin-escape

:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`return value depends on the object referenced by`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`{diagtext}`, not on '*this'`
:::

Experimental. Detects member functions returning a value derived from a
pointer, reference, or view field rather than from ``*this``. May report owned
pointer fields (e.g., ``Vector::data()``), which can be silenced by marking the
method ``[[clang::lifetimebound]]``.

(-Wformat-non-iso)=

### -Wformat-non-iso

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

    :::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

:::

(-Wframe-larger-than)=

### -Wframe-larger-than

This diagnostic is enabled by default.

**Diagnostic text:**

The text of this diagnostic is not controlled by Clang.

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`stack frame size (`{placeholder}`A`{diagtext}`) exceeds limit (`{placeholder}`B`{diagtext}`) in '`{placeholder}`C`{diagtext}`'`
:::

More fine grained information about the stack layout is available by adding the
`-Rpass-analysis=stack-frame-layout` command-line flag to the compiler
invocation.

The diagnostic information can be saved to a file in a machine readable format,
like YAML by adding the `-foptimization-record-file=<file>` command-line flag.

Results can be filtered by function name by passing
`-mllvm -filter-print-funcs=foo`, where `foo` is the target function's name.

   ```console
   clang -c a.cpp -Rpass-analysis=stack-frame-layout -mllvm -filter-print-funcs=foo
   ```

   ```console
   clang -c a.cpp -Rpass-analysis=stack-frame-layout -foptimization-record-file=<file>
   ```

(-Wframe-larger-than=)=

### -Wframe-larger-than=

Synonym for {ref}`-Wframe-larger-than`.

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {error}`error:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`binding type 'c' ignored in buffer declaration. Did you mean 'packoffset'?`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`binding type '`
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`t`
    * - {diagtext}`u`
    * - {diagtext}`b`
    * - {diagtext}`s`
    * - {diagtext}`c`
    :::
  - {diagtext}`' only applies to types containing`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`SRV resources`
    * - {diagtext}`UAV resources`
    * - {diagtext}`constant buffer resources`
    * - {diagtext}`sampler state`
    * - {diagtext}`numeric types`
    :::
:::


(-Wliblto)=

### -Wliblto

This diagnostic flag exists for GCC compatibility, and has no effect in Clang.

(-Wlifetime-safety)=

### -Wlifetime-safety

Controls {ref}`-Wlifetime-safety-permissive`, {ref}`-Wlifetime-safety-strict`.

Warnings to detect use-after-free and related temporal safety bugs based on lifetime safety analysis.
  

(-Wlifetime-safety-all)=

### -Wlifetime-safety-all

Controls {ref}`-Wlifetime-safety`, {ref}`-Wlifetime-safety-suggestions`, {ref}`-Wlifetime-safety-validations`.

Turns on all the warnings in the lifetime-safety umbrella.
  

(-Wlifetime-safety-annotation-placement)=

### -Wlifetime-safety-annotation-placement

Controls {ref}`-Wlifetime-safety-inapplicable-lifetimebound`, {ref}`-Wlifetime-safety-misplaced-lifetimebound`.

Validates that lifetime annotations are placed on appropriate types and in appropriate locations.
  

(-Wlifetime-safety-annotation-verification)=

### -Wlifetime-safety-annotation-verification

Controls {ref}`-Wlifetime-safety-lifetimebound-violation`, {ref}`-Wlifetime-safety-noescape`.

Verifies that function implementations adhere to their lifetime annotation contracts through dataflow analysis.

(-Wlifetime-safety-dangling-field)=

### -Wlifetime-safety-dangling-field

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`stack memory associated with`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`escapes to the`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`&nbsp;{diagtext}`which will dangle`
:::

Warning to detect dangling field references.
  

(-Wlifetime-safety-dangling-field-lambda-capture)=

### -Wlifetime-safety-dangling-field-lambda-capture

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`stack memory associated with`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`may escape to the`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`&nbsp;{diagtext}`which will dangle. This could be a false positive as the field was captured by a lambda and may have been reset before escaping`
:::

Warning to detect dangling field references.
This may contain false-positives, e.g. when the field is captured by a lambda that resets the field before function exit.
  

(-Wlifetime-safety-dangling-field-moved)=

### -Wlifetime-safety-dangling-field-moved

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`stack memory associated with`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`may escape to the`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`&nbsp;{diagtext}`which will dangle. This could be a false positive as the storage may have been moved. Consider moving first and then aliasing later to resolve the issue`
:::

Warning to detect dangling field references.
This may contain false-positives, e.g. when the borrowed storage is potentially moved and is not destroyed at function exit.

(-Wlifetime-safety-inapplicable-lifetimebound)=

### -Wlifetime-safety-inapplicable-lifetimebound

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`'lifetimebound' attribute has no effect on parameter of type`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`{diagtext}`. The attribute only applies to reference types, pointer types, and non-owner record types`
:::

Detects uses of [[clang::lifetimebound]] that have no effect because the type of the annotated parameter cannot carry a lifetime.

(-Wlifetime-safety-lifetimebound-violation)=

### -Wlifetime-safety-lifetimebound-violation

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`could not verify that the return value can be lifetime bound to`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`an unnamed parameter`
    * - {diagtext}`'`{placeholder}`B`{diagtext}`'`
    * - {diagtext}`the implicit this parameter`
    :::
:::

Detects parameters marked as [[clang::lifetimebound]] for which the analysis could not verify that the return value can be lifetime bound to the parameter.
This warning may produce false-positives diagnostics when it cannot fully model the code.
  

(-Wlifetime-safety-misplaced-lifetimebound)=

Detects function definitions whose parameters or implicit this argument are marked as [[clang::lifetimebound]] when the first declaration is not.

(-Wmax-tokens)=

### -Wmax-tokens

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`the number of preprocessor source tokens (`{placeholder}`A`{diagtext}`) exceeds this token limit (`{placeholder}`B`{diagtext}`)`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`the total number of preprocessor source tokens (`{placeholder}`A`{diagtext}`) exceeds the token limit (`{placeholder}`B`{diagtext}`)`
:::

The warning is issued if the number of pre-processor tokens exceeds
the token limit, which can be set in three ways:

1. As a limit at a specific point in a file, using the `clang max_tokens_here`
   pragma:

   ```c++
   #pragma clang max_tokens_here 1234
   ```

2. As a per-translation unit limit, using the `-fmax-tokens=` command-line
   flag:

   ```console
   clang -c a.cpp -fmax-tokens=1234
   ```

3. As a per-translation unit limit using the `clang max_tokens_total` pragma,
   which works like and overrides the `-fmax-tokens=` flag:

   ```c++
   #pragma clang max_tokens_total 1234
   ```

These limits can be helpful in limiting code growth through included files.

Setting a token limit of zero means no limit.

Note that the warning is disabled by default, so -Wmax-tokens must be used
in addition with the pragmas or -fmax-tokens flag to get any warnings.

(-Wmax-unsigned-zero)=

### -Wmax-unsigned-zero

This diagnostic is enabled by default.

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`taking the max of`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`a value and unsigned zero`
    * - {diagtext}`unsigned zero and a value`
    :::
  - &nbsp;{diagtext}`is always equal to the other value`
:::

### -Wmicrosoft

Some of the diagnostics controlled by this flag are enabled by default.

Controls {ref}`-Winconsistent-dllimport`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-abstract`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-anon-tag`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-cast`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-charize`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-comment-paste`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-const-init`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-cpp-macro`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-default-arg-redefinition`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-drectve-section`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-empty-enum`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-end-of-file`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-enum-forward-reference`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-enum-value`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-exception-spec`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-explicit-constructor-call`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-extra-qualification`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-fixed-enum`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-flexible-array`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-goto`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-include`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-init-from-predefined`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-inline-on-non-function`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-mutable-reference`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-pure-definition`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-redeclare-static`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-sealed`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-string-literal-from-predefined`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-template`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-union-member-reference`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-unqualified-friend`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-using-decl`, {ref}`-Wmicrosoft-void-pseudo-dtor`.


(-Wmicrosoft-abstract)=

### -Wmicrosoft-abstract

This diagnostic is enabled by default.

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`'abstract' keyword is a Microsoft extension`
:::

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

:::

:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`use of member`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`found via unqualified lookup into dependent bases of class templates is a Microsoft extension`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`use of member`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`before its declaration is a Microsoft extension`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`using the undeclared type`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`as a default template argument is a Microsoft extension`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`non-type template argument containing a dereference operation is a Microsoft extension`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`class template`
    * - {diagtext}`class template partial`
    * - {diagtext}`variable template`
    * - {diagtext}`variable template partial`
    * - {diagtext}`function template`
    * - {diagtext}`member function`
    * - {diagtext}`static data member`
    * - {diagtext}`member class`
    * - {diagtext}`member enumeration`
    :::
  - &nbsp;{diagtext}`specialization of`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`&nbsp;{diagtext}`not in`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`a namespace enclosing`&nbsp;{placeholder}`C`
    * - {diagtext}`class`&nbsp;{placeholder}`C`&nbsp;{diagtext}`or an enclosing namespace`
    :::
  - &nbsp;{diagtext}`is a Microsoft extension`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`template argument for template type parameter must be a type; omitted 'typename' is a Microsoft extension`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`'static' can only be specified inside the class definition`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

(-Wms-bitfield-padding)=

### -Wms-bitfield-padding

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`bit-field`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`of type`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`&nbsp;{diagtext}`has a different storage size than the preceding bit-field (`{placeholder}`C`&nbsp;{diagtext}`vs`&nbsp;{placeholder}`D`&nbsp;{diagtext}`bytes) and will not be packed under the Microsoft ABI`
:::

Under the Microsoft ABI, adjacent bit-fields are not packed if the
underlying type has a different storage size. This warning indicates that a
pair of adjacent bit-fields may not pack in the same way due to this behavioural
difference.

This can occur when mixing different types explicitly:

```c++
struct S {
  uint16_t field1 : 1;
  uint32_t field2 : 1;
};
```

or more subtly through enums

```c++
enum Enum1 { /* ... */ };
enum class Enum2 : unsigned char { /* ... */ };
struct S {
  Enum1 field1 : 1;
  Enum2 field2 : 1;
};
```

In each of these cases under the Microsoft ABI the second bit-field
will not be packed with the preceding bit-field, and instead will be aligned
as if the fields were each separately defined integer fields of their respective
storage size. For binary compatibility this is obviously and observably
incompatible, however where bit-fields are being used solely for memory use
reduction this incomplete packing may silently increase the size of objects vs
what is expected.

This issue can be addressed by ensuring the storage type of each bit-field is
the same, either by explicitly using the same integer type, or in the case of
enum types declaring the enum types with the same storage size. For enum types
where you cannot specify the underlying type, the options are to either switch
to int sized storage for all specifiers or to resort to declaring the
bit-fields with explicit integer storage types and cast in and out of the field.
If such a solution is required the
{ref}`preferred_type <langext-preferred_type_documentation>` attribute can be
used to convey the actual field type to debuggers and other tooling.

(-Wnan-infinity-disabled)=

### -Wnan-infinity-disabled

This diagnostic is enabled by default.

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`use of`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`infinity`
    * - {diagtext}`NaN`
    :::
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * -
    * - &nbsp;{diagtext}`via a macro`
    :::
  - &nbsp;{diagtext}`is undefined behavior due to the currently enabled floating-point options`
:::

This warning is enabled when source code using the macros `INFINITY` or `NAN`
is compiled with floating-point options preventing these two values. This can
lead to undefined behavior. Check the order of command line arguments that modify
this behavior, such as `-ffast-math`, `-fhonor-infinities`, and
`-fhonor-nans` (etc), as well as `#pragma` directives if this diagnostic is
generated unexpectedly.

:::

(-Wopenmp-target)=

### -Wopenmp-target

This diagnostic is enabled by default.

Also controls {ref}`-Wopenmp-mapping`.

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

(-Wparentheses)=

### -Wparentheses

Some of the diagnostics controlled by this flag are enabled by default.

Also controls {ref}`-Wbitwise-conditional-parentheses`, {ref}`-Wbitwise-op-parentheses`, {ref}`-Wdangling-else`, {ref}`-Wlogical-not-parentheses`, {ref}`-Wlogical-op-parentheses`, {ref}`-Woverloaded-shift-op-parentheses`, {ref}`-Wparentheses-equality`, {ref}`-Wshift-op-parentheses`.

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {error}`error:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`comparison in fold expression would evaluate to '(X`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`Y)`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`Z' which does not behave the same as a mathematical expression`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`using the result of an assignment as a condition without parentheses`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {error}`error:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`chained comparison 'X`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`Y`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`&nbsp;{diagtext}`Z' does not behave the same as a mathematical expression`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`has lower precedence than`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`{diagtext}`;`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`&nbsp;{diagtext}`will be evaluated first`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`operator '?:' has lower precedence than '`{placeholder}`A`{diagtext}`'; '`{placeholder}`A`{diagtext}`' will be evaluated first`
:::

(-Rpass-analysis)=

### -Rpass-analysis

**Diagnostic text:**

The text of this diagnostic is not controlled by Clang.

:::{list-table}

* - {remark}`remark:`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`{diagtext}`; allow reordering by specifying '#pragma clang loop vectorize(enable)' before the loop; if the arrays will always be independent, specify '#pragma clang loop vectorize(assume_safety)' before the loop or provide the '__restrict__' qualifier with the independent array arguments -- erroneous results will occur if these options are incorrectly applied`
:::

(-Wpedantic-core-features)=

### -Wpedantic-core-features

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`is a core feature in`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`OpenCL C`
    * - {diagtext}`C++ for OpenCL`
    :::
  - &nbsp;{diagtext}`version`&nbsp;{placeholder}`C`&nbsp;{diagtext}`but not supported on this target`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`OpenCL extension`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`is core feature or supported optional core feature - ignoring`
:::


(-Wpedantic-macros)=

### -Wpedantic-macros

This diagnostic is enabled by default.

Controls {ref}`-Wbuiltin-macro-redefined`, {ref}`-Wdeprecated-pragma`, {ref}`-Wfinal-macro`, {ref}`-Wmacro-redefined`, {ref}`-Wrestrict-expansion`.

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`function`

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`alias declaration in this context is incompatible with C++ standards before C++23`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`'auto' as a functional-style cast is incompatible with C++ standards before C++23`

:widths: auto

:widths: auto

  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`thread_local`
    :::

    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`function`
    * - {diagtext}`constructor`
    :::
  - &nbsp;{diagtext}`is incompatible with C++ standards before C++23`
:::

:widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`constructor`
    :::

    * - {diagtext}`elifdef`
    * - {diagtext}`elifndef`
    :::

:widths: auto

(-Wrange-loop-bind-reference)=

### -Wrange-loop-bind-reference

**Diagnostic text:**

(-Wtautological-compare)=

### -Wtautological-compare

Some of the diagnostics controlled by this flag are enabled by default.

Also controls {ref}`-Wtautological-bitwise-compare`, {ref}`-Wtautological-constant-compare`, {ref}`-Wtautological-negation-compare`, {ref}`-Wtautological-objc-bool-compare`, {ref}`-Wtautological-overlap-compare`, {ref}`-Wtautological-pointer-compare`, {ref}`-Wtautological-undefined-compare`.

:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`aligning a value`
    * - {diagtext}`the result of checking whether a value is aligned`
    :::
  - &nbsp;{diagtext}`to 1 byte is`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`a no-op`
    * - {diagtext}`always true`
    :::
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`self-`
    * - {diagtext}`array`&nbsp;
    * - {diagtext}`pointer`&nbsp;
    :::
  - {diagtext}`comparison always evaluates to`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`a constant`
    * - {diagtext}`true`
    * - {diagtext}`false`
    * - {diagtext}`'std::strong_ordering::equal'`
    :::
:::

(-Wthread-safety-attributes)=

### -Wthread-safety-attributes

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

:::

:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`only applies to pointer types; type here is`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`

:widths: auto

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`attribute without capability arguments refers to 'this', but`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`&nbsp;{diagtext}`isn't annotated with 'capability' or 'scoped_lockable' attribute`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`attribute on a`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`variable`
    * - {diagtext}`field`
    :::
  - &nbsp;{diagtext}`requires the`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`variable`
    * - {diagtext}`field`
    :::
  - &nbsp;{diagtext}`to be of function pointer type`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`attribute without capability arguments can only be applied to non-static methods of a class`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`attribute applies to function parameters only if their type is a function pointer or a reference to a 'scoped_lockable'-annotated type`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

(-Wunique-object-duplication)=

### -Wunique-object-duplication

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`initialization of`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`may run twice when built into a shared library: it has external linkage and`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`hidden visibility`
    * - {diagtext}`no import/export annotation`
    :::
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`may be duplicated when built into a shared library: it is mutable, with external linkage and`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`hidden visibility`
    * - {diagtext}`no import/export annotation`
    :::
:::

Warns when objects which are supposed to be globally unique might get duplicated
when built into a shared library.

This can occur to objects which are hidden from the dynamic linker, due to
having hidden visibility (on posix) or lacking a dllimport/dllexport attribute
(on windows). If such an object is built into a shared library, each instance
of the library will get its own copy. This can cause very subtle bugs if there was
only supposed to be one copy of the object in question: singletons aren't single,
changes to one object won't affect the others, the object's initializer will run
once per copy, etc.

Specifically, this warning fires when it detects an object which:

1. Is defined as `inline` in a header file (so it might get compiled into multiple libaries), and
1. Has external linkage (otherwise it's supposed to be duplicated), and
1. Has hidden visibility (posix) or lacks a dllimport/dllexport attribute (windows).

As well as one of the following:

1. The object is mutable, or
1. The object's initializer definitely has side effects.

The warning can be resolved by removing one of the conditions above. In rough
order of preference, this may be done by:

1. Marking the object `const` (if possible)
1. Moving the object's definition to a source file
1. Making the object visible using `__attribute((visibility("default")))`,
   `__declspec(dllimport)`, or `__declspec(dllexport)`.

When annotating an object with `__declspec(dllimport)` or `__declspec(dllexport)`,
take care to ensure that the object is only exported from one dll, and is imported
everywhere else.

Note that for (2), all levels of a pointer variable must be constant;
`const int*` will trigger the warning because the pointer itself is mutable.

(-Wunnecessary-virtual-specifier)=

### -Wunnecessary-virtual-specifier

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`virtual method`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`is inside a 'final' class and can never be overridden`
:::

Warns when a `final` class contains a virtual method (including virtual
destructors) that does not override anything. Since `final` classes cannot
be subclassed, their methods cannot be overridden, so there is no point to
introducing new `virtual` methods.

The warning also detects virtual methods in classes whose destructor is
`final`, for the same reason.

(-Wvarargs)=

### -Wvarargs

This diagnostic is enabled by default.

**Diagnostic text:**

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`second argument to 'va_start' is not the last non-variadic parameter`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`second argument to 'va_arg' is of array type`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`{diagtext}`; this va_arg has undefined behavior because arguments will never be compatible with array type`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`second argument to 'va_arg' is of promotable type`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`{diagtext}`; this va_arg has undefined behavior because arguments will be promoted to`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`
:::

:::{list-table}
:widths: auto

* - {warning}`warning:`&nbsp;{diagtext}`passing`&nbsp;
  - :::{list-table}
    :widths: auto

    * - {diagtext}`an object that undergoes default argument promotion`
    * - {diagtext}`an object of reference type`
    * - {diagtext}`a parameter declared with the 'register' keyword`
    :::
  - &nbsp;{diagtext}`to 'va_start' has undefined behavior`
:::

        :widths: auto

    * - :::{list-table}
        :widths: auto

        * - {diagtext}`converting`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`to type`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`
        * - {diagtext}`converting between types`
        :::
    * - :::{list-table}
        :widths: auto

        * - {diagtext}`initializing`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`with an expression of type`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`
        * - {diagtext}`initializing with expression of different type`
        :::
    * - :::{list-table}
        :widths: auto

        * - {diagtext}`sending`&nbsp;{placeholder}`A`&nbsp;{diagtext}`to parameter of type`&nbsp;{placeholder}`B`
        * - {diagtext}`sending to parameter of different type`

        :widths: auto

:::


(-Wwrite-strings)=

### -Wwrite-strings

Synonym for {ref}`-Wwritable-strings`.

**Note:** enabling this warning in C will change the semantic behavior of the
program by treating all string literals as having type `const char *`
instead of `char *`. This can cause unexpected behaviors with type-sensitive
constructs like `_Generic`.
